//: Spawn N actors of one def, for one faction, in a DISTANCE BAND around a reference point. Distance is a SEARCH CONSTRAINT, not a promise: the plan reports the achieved distance of every actor it placed.
//needs: a tactical mission that is PLAYING, and - unless useCenter is true - a SELECTED actor to measure from (@selected). Nothing selected = the anchor step fails and says so.
//center: useCenter true + centerX/centerY/centerZ measures from an explicit world point instead of the selected actor.
//caps: `repeat times` must be a literal in this engine, so 12 actors and 12 position tries per actor are HARD ceilings here; `count` below that is honoured through the `while` guard.

steps.//: THE REFERENCE POINT. Exactly one of these two runs, and both save to ANCHOR.

steps.//PRELOAD: MANDATORY, and the reason a squad used to spawn INVISIBLE. The `spawn` console command does the whole spawn INSIDE the loading callback (TacticalDeployZone.cs:424 -> onLoadingCompleted at :409-423): a def whose addressable assets are not resident yet produces a live, in-play, correctly-positioned actor with no model. Assets are per-DEF, so this only looked unnecessary when the def was already on the map.

steps.//: LoadRoots (AssetsReferencesLoader.cs:71) rather than StartLoadingRoots (:58): it is the SAME acquisition - it calls StartLoadingRoots itself, so the level's own Dispose (TacticalLevelController.cs:416) still releases what we take - but it is an iterator that only ends once _loadCrts is empty. That is what gives us something to wait ON. This is the game's own idiom (TacticalLevelController.cs:557-569).

Timing.Start(coroutine, catchException) (Timing.cs:246) hands back the IUpdateable whose Stopped is a POSITIVE, live, single-call completion predicate. The plan engine has no `not`, and AssetsReferencesLoader.IsLoading / AssetsManager.IsLoading() are both the wrong polarity AND loader-global; Stopped is neither. The explicit null is the optional catchException - the binder matches arity exactly.
ASYNCHRONOUS. Spawning on the next round-trip would wait for nothing at all - which is exactly what the old sequence did.
def -> (ComponentSetDef, ActorInstanceData). SpawnActor CLONES the instance data (TacticalDeployZone.cs:258-268), so one pair serves every actor in the squad.

THE DISTANCE BAND, as the engine's own ring generator (TacticalMap.cs:446). It is a lazy iterator and purely geometric - no floor and no nav knowledge - so every candidate still has to be snapped and CanStandAt-ed.
Materialize it: GetRandomElement wants an ICollection (UnityUtil.cs:414), and a lazy iterator is not one.

The accumulator. The plan engine has no list building, so the game holds it: one ArrayList of one interpolated line per actor. `new ArrayList()` is refused as ambiguous against the static .cctor, hence the capacity ctor.
ONE PASS PER ACTOR. `times` must be a literal here, so 12 is the ceiling and the `while` guard is what honours `count`.

SEARCH: a random ring candidate, snapped to a floor, gated on the engine's own CanStandAt. Random rather than indexed because the engine has no loop variable - and it also spreads the squad instead of clustering it at the ring's first cell.
Probe from ABOVE the floor: SnapXYZ casts down onto the mask.
The engine has no `not` and `repeat` has no `until`, so the negation is a real call. Object.Equals(false, x) is the shortest one that always resolves.
An ASSERTION written as a one-shot wait: the search loop exiting proves nothing on its own, and spawning into a wall must be a named failure rather than a silent bad placement.
TacticalDeployZone.cs:415 really does assign the actor to its own Source.
REQUESTED-VS-ACHIEVED, per actor, recorded where the plan engine can carry it: one interpolated line into the ArrayList.
The `while` guard: keep spawning while fewer than `count` lines have been recorded.

The housekeeping `spawn` does after its own spawn (TacticalDeployZone.cs:421-422), once for the whole squad rather than once per actor. StartTurn is deliberately NOT called - the command only does it when the new actor's faction is the level's CurrentFaction.

COSMETIC TAIL, and onError:continue is load-bearing. ResetCharacterSelectedState re-runs selection, which asks the navmesh for a path; while the map is rebuilding (in-combat explosions) it throws InvalidOperationException: 'Map is updating, cannot calculate path!'. The squad is already spawned and in play by then, so letting that invert the plan's verdict reported FAILED over completed work - and a false FAILED invites spawning everything twice. It is a WARNING now: the step is still traced with its error, and `selectionReset` in the output says whether it took.

finally.//: The preload intermediates. The ASSETS stay held on purpose - the loader owns them and the level releases them on teardown; only these handles go.
